column1: # The registry of recorded reviews that dev/review-coverage reads: one row per review, the
# commits it read, the paths it read, and the DECISIONS.md heading that records it. The format
# is the tool's header's (`dev/review-coverage --help`); `--check` holds every row, and
# tooling-tests/dev_review_coverage.rs runs it at every gate.
# A review's row is added by the record commit that closes it, with its DECISIONS.md entry,
# or at the merge that brings that entry into the tree (the plan before the opening, section 1,
# "Every review registers what it read"). A row covers exactly what its review read.

column4: 2026-10-07 — The `test` half of the stabilization workflow, re-reviewed: fit for a canary run and not yet for the real run — 3 HIGH, 15 MEDIUM and 18 LOW from two reviewers, every HIGH and MEDIUM driven again and none refuted, and its second repair planned as six structural changes (a record and a plan: nothing built and nothing ruled — five questions are the human's)

2026-10-18 — Silence 13 was no silence: a file staged on an unborn `HEAD` is tracked, and the design docs refuse it — its cell is listed as refused and holds, its key retires, and the one sentence that says otherwise is a guide's (the byte table, task `B6`, after its review: the first of its fixes)

2026-10-18 — The base-pin rule hid a loss: a staged doc gone from a unit whose pin stands is *lost* again, and the one move the frame lets go is the re-slug — `W4`'s own word, the same lines under a new name in the same task, its `# H1` rewritten (the byte table, task `B6`, after the family's review: the first of its fixes)

2026-10-18 — Three sets the comparison reads a line through answer to the unit the command acts on: a copy a line lets land is of a doc staged in that unit, the staged docs held to a commit are every unit's and every merged set's together, and a fan-out's commit holds what the sub-tasks' worktrees staged and no other checkout's — red first on six cases, and no classification moved on either binary (the byte table, task `B7`, after part A's review: the first of its fixes)

2026-10-19 — The config layer a finalize carries is carried on the layer's first commit alone, at both doors that quote the sentence: `M3, the config` held under any `HEAD`, so a file of the user's nobody staged under `.jigc/config`, swept into a landed boundary, held — and whether a pending delta rides a later commit is no answered question but two docs saying two things, entry 19, open; one cell moved and one is added, each red on both binaries under a key of its door (the byte table, task B7, after part B's review: the first of its fixes)

2026-10-19 — Every repository the suite makes is still once git returns: `maintenance.auto` and `gc.auto` off, by the environment cargo gives every process, which closes the `copy_tree` flake of the run's opening ledger and the failure of `record_door_baseline` in B8's gates (the byte table, task B8, after its review: the first of its fixes)

2026-10-20 — The rulings of 2026-10-20 are held at `relocate`'s own door: a refusal of the whole sweep is not the outcome its second-note cells list, and an occupant at a new home has a cell with a second note (the byte table, task B9, after its review: the first of its fixes)

2026-10-26 — A cache's own file is the only thing a cache's line lets stand at its place: no directory made at `edges.json`, `file-state.json` or a milestone's `base.json` and `tasks.json` inside a directory a line names, and no cache file written over a link, a directory or a special file of the user's; red first, and no cell moved on either binary (the byte table, task B10, after its review: the first of its fixes)

2026-10-28 — The review of the link-on-the-way guard: every finding fixed, red first — a read form reports and never refuses, one code for the state at `setup` and the root knobs, a route chosen by where the link leads, and no link jigc parks or follows (before the stabilization run's opening: no write through a link on the way)

2026-10-28 — The re-review of the link-on-the-way guard: *wrote nothing* true at the write primitives, the advisory inside a JSON document, and four more doors held to the rule (before the stabilization run's opening: no write through a link on the way)

2026-10-28 — The second re-review of the link-on-the-way guard: a dry run refuses as its act does, the teardown passes a link to nothing and asks the hook, and nothing is parked past a link (the human's ruling A: a fourth cycle; before the stabilization run's opening: no write through a link on the way)

2026-10-28 — The third re-review of the link-on-the-way guard: two regressions closed, `setup`'s hook route names the link, and eight keys recorded for the ledger (the human's ruling: no merge over a known regression; before the stabilization run's opening: no write through a link on the way)
